deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84): Grothendieck is studying a 'système de pseudo-droites', a finite arrangement K of pseudolines in a projective plane X with its induced cell decomposition. In that decomposition faces F are polygons whose boundaries split into cells; the 'grandes cellules' are the full sides. Each face carries a distribution of signs ε_F(α) attached to the cells α of ∂F. The previous page proves a local proposition. Take two faces F and F' = σ_a(F) adjacent along a side a. (i) The sides of F that remain sides of F' form an arc A. (ii) On the complementary arc B there are three possible configurations (cases 1°, 2°, 3°, with numbers of sides (3,2), (3,3), (3,4)). (iii) For α in A with α ≠ a, the sign is unchanged: ε_{F'}(α) = ε_F(α). (iv) On the shared side the sign flips: ε_{F'}(a) = -ε_F(a).

This page draws the consequences.

Corollary 1: in every case the sign distribution on F determines the one on F'.
- Cases 1° and 3° are asymmetric: one knows which of F, F' is the 'specialisation' of the other, and that settles the signs on B.
- Case 2° is symmetric, so a finer argument is given. One kind of side ('cotation') carries equal signs for F and F'; this holds in all cases. The remaining sides come in pairs whose signs are opposite for F and F'. Their counts are (1,0), (1,1) or (1,2) according to the case.

Corollary 2: the dual graph of X is connected. So knowing the signs ε_F for one face gives them for all faces, by propagating across adjacent faces.

Caveat: the proof implicitly assumed that neither F nor F' is an 'exceptional' face, i.e. one coming from an exceptional relative position (word unclear, perhaps 'supracritique'). Such faces need separate treatment; for them the side count differs and the sign distribution seems directly known.

Conclusion: this gives a simple description of the signs in terms of the bare combinatorial structure (X, K, S_K) alone. It avoids the 'arcs critiques' used on the previous page, and even the auxiliary graph L ⊂ X.

In modern terms: a sign labelling on the cells of a pseudoline arrangement is defined by a local transition rule across edges of the dual (tope) graph. Since that graph is connected, the labelling is rigid: determined by its value on one tope. This is the standard mechanism behind the fact that the cell complex determines sign data up to a global choice (oriented matroids of rank 3, Folkman–Lawrence representation).
errors: The exceptional faces are explicitly not covered by the proof, so Corollaries 1-2 are established only modulo that check. Grothendieck flags this himself.

Propagation by connectivity needs the local rule to be path-independent (consistency around each vertex/cycle of the dual graph) for the labelling to be well defined. Here the signs are presumably defined globally beforehand, so propagation only proves uniqueness. That is fine, but existence/consistency is not addressed if the rule is meant as a definition.
Line 'y compris dans les cas 1° et 2°' probably should read '1° et 3°' (slip of pen, or misreading).

ideas.what: Local transition rule for face sign data across a common side (sign of the shared side flips, other common sides keep their sign, three configurations on the complementary arc)
ideas.modern_name: sign-vector / covector change across a wall in a pseudoline arrangement (oriented matroid rank 3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folkman–Lawrence 1978; Bland–Las Vergnas; Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler book

ideas.what: Global determination of signs from one face via connectivity of the arrangement complex
ideas.modern_name: rigidity of labellings along the connected tope graph; tope graph determines the oriented matroid up to reorientation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Björner–Edelman–Ziegler 1990 (tope graph result); propagation argument folklore

ideas.what: Aim of describing the signs purely from the combinatorial structure (X,K,S_K), without auxiliary critical arcs or the graph L
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial/intrinsic characterisation of sign data of pseudoline arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: oriented matroid theory (Goodman–Pollack allowable sequences, wiring diagrams)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's pseudoline work is only mentioned in passing in Récoltes et Semailles / correspondence (unsure of details)

missed.claim: The case of exceptional faces (exceptional relative positions) is left unchecked. Corollaries 1-2 remain conditional on it in these notes.
missed.quote: J'ai supposé implicitement dans les vérifications de la proposition que ni F, ni F' n'était une face exceptionnelle
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It only completes an internal argument whose analogue is standard in oriented matroid theory.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine propagation argument (local wall-crossing rule plus connectivity). It belongs to Grothendieck's little-known pseudoline programme, but its mathematical content is standard in oriented matroid theory. Its interest is mainly historical, as evidence of Grothendieck independently developing rank-3 oriented matroid combinatorics.
transcription_corrections: 'sans avoir à utiliser les axes cartésiens' should read 'sans avoir à utiliser les arcs critiques' (consistent with the previous page's 'arcs critiques').
'i.e. "suprapolaire"' is uncertain; the image looks more like '"supracritiques"' / '"supercritiques"'.
'quatre[?] deux[?] autres cotations' is uncertain; possibly 'deux sortes de cotations'.
'y compris dans les cas 1° et 2°' is likely '1° et 3°' in intent.

'il n'y a pas quatre grandes faces, et la distribution des signes autres' probably reads '... grandes faces, et la distribution des signes ... est connue'; the duplicated line 'autres[?], et la distribution des signes' is a transcription artefact.
'seule[?] structure de[?] contexte de (X,K,S_K)' probably reads '(en fonction de la) seule structure de (X, K, S_K)'.
